=You filter keyword ideas for the blog of a B2B AI automation agency. The target reader is a business owner or operations leader who is evaluating or planning to implement AI automation in their company to save time or cost. Keep a keyword only if that person would plausibly search it.

Remove keywords whose searcher is a learner or job seeker (courses, certificates, beginner tutorials, jobs), a developer (code, github, open source setup), a consumer or hobbyist (chatbots with no restrictions, free AI app lists, top AI apps, roleplay), or someone looking for forum threads (reddit). Remove brand navigation queries.

Also remove keywords that ask for free tools, general consumer productivity or tool roundups unrelated to business automation, and single broad head terms such as "ai automation".

Return only JSON in this exact shape: {"keep": ["keyword one", "keyword two"]}
Use each keyword exactly as written.

Keywords to judge:

parameters.content:
## KEWORD RESEARCH
Runs automatically once a week.

Pull data — Searches Google for keywords using a broad seed and gets ~90 results with search volume, difficulty, and buyer intent.
Filter — Removes keywords with too little search volume, too much competition, or the wrong intent.
Check relevance — AI reviews the list and keeps only keywords a real business buyer would search (drops student, developer, and hobbyist searches).
Score — Ranks keywords by how realistic they are to rank for right now, favoring easier wins over pure search volume.
Remove duplicates — Checks against past weeks so we never repeat a keyword already used.
Fill gaps — If too few new keywords are found, pulls fresh related terms instead of reusing old ones.
Finalize — Picks the top 5, assigns one to each weekday (Monday-Friday), and saves them to the spreadsheet.

## COMPETITOR ANALYSIS 
Runs after the 5 keywords are ranked and saved. For each keyword, researches what's already ranking on Google and extracts a content brief.

Flow: GetSERP (pulls top 10 Google results per keyword) → ParseSERP (keeps organic results, drops Reddit/YouTube/ads, captures People Also Ask) → SplitByResult → TrimToTop3 (keeps only the top 3 competitor pages per keyword) → FetchCompetitorPages (downloads each page, errors routed to HandleFetchErrors as a fallback) → ExtractArticleText (pulls readable text from the page HTML) → RestoreKeywordFields (re-attaches keyword/url/title lost during extraction) → Merge (combines successful fetches with fallback data) → TrimBodyText (caps each page's text to stay within AI token limits) → GroupByKeyword (groups the 3 pages back under their keyword) → CompetitorBrief (AI reads the 3 competitor pages and outputs shared subtopics, content gaps, and recommended headings) → SaveBrief (writes the brief to the sheet).

## CONTENT CREATION & DISTRIBUTION
Runs after the competitor brief is saved. Drafts a blog post per keyword, holds it for editor approval, then publishes and repurposes it once approved.

Flow: DraftBlogPost (GPT-4.1 writes a 1200-1800 word B2B post from the brief's headings, subtopics, and gaps) → MergeKeywordRow (re-attaches keyword row, draft, and headings) → UpdateDraftStatus (saves draft to the sheet as pending_approval) → DailyPostTrigger (9am Mon-Fri) → GetTodayPost (pulls the row scheduled for today with pending_approval status) → SendApprovalEmail (emails the draft and waits for the editor's free-text reply) → CheckApproval (approved goes to the True branch, anything else to the False branch). If edits are requested: ReviseDraft (Gemini rewrites the draft using the editor's notes) → Edit Fields (puts the revision into draft_content) → back to SendApprovalEmail. If approved, three parallel branches: PublishWebsite (posts keyword and draft to the site endpoint) → UpdateStatus (marks the row Published); RepurposeLinkedIn (Gemini condenses the draft into a LinkedIn post); RepurposeNewsletter (Gemini condenses the draft into a newsletter section) → PublishNewsletter (emails it via Gmail).
